title: Prefer `json_validate()` over decode-and-check
summary: `json_validate()`, added in PHP 8.3, reports whether a string is syntactically valid JSON without building the decoded value, replacing the common `json_decode()` plus `json_last_error()` validity check.
new_code_policy: When new code only needs to know whether a string is valid JSON, call `json_validate($json, $depth, $flags)` instead of decoding it and inspecting `json_last_error()`.
existing_code_policy: When touching an existing decode-and-check validity test, replace it with `json_validate()` using the same `$depth`/`$flags` the old `json_decode()` call used; leave the code alone when the decoded value itself is used for anything beyond the validity check.
guideline: Use `json_validate()` to test whether a string is valid JSON; keep `json_decode()` for call sites that also need the decoded value.
details: PHP 8.3 added `json_validate(string $json, int $depth = 512, int $flags = 0): bool`, which parses just far enough to report whether `$json` is syntactically valid JSON and never builds the resulting PHP value. The pre-8.3 idiom for the same yes/no question is `json_decode($json)` followed by `json_last_error() === JSON_ERROR_NONE`, which always constructs (and then discards) the full decoded value just to test validity. Here `introduced_in` is set to `8.3` because that is the minor `json_validate()` itself became available in - the field exists so this modern_preference rule can be range-gated on the feature axis, not because PHP 8.3 introduced JSON validation as a concept, and it is not a lifecycle claim about the older decode-and-check idiom this rule prefers away from. `json_validate()` shares `json_decode()`'s default `$depth` of 512, so a plain rewrite with no explicit depth/flags preserves the original depth behavior; a call site that passed a custom `$depth` or decode options to `json_decode()` must carry the equivalent `$depth`/`$flags` into `json_validate()` to keep the same validity semantics.
notes: This rule applies only when the decoded value is discarded after the validity check; when the code also uses the decoded value, `json_decode()` remains correct and the second, no-automatic-replacement example applies instead.

`json_validate()` and `json_decode()` accept the same `$depth`/flags shape, so a custom `$depth` or decode option on the original `json_decode()` call must be reproduced on `json_validate()` to keep identical validity behavior.

Evidence: UPGRADING-8.3.0.txt, '6. New Functions' -> JSON: 'Added json_validate(), which returns whether the json is valid for the given $depth and $options.' No mention of json_validate() in the 8.2, 8.4 or 8.5 UPGRADING files, so no deprecation or removal is on record.
